task: Alpha Memory Implementation Step 1 -- Stable phi Identity + Cross-Run History Reader (SHADOW ONLY)
head: 9f228723fad5406c72e62beca67ec70ea0fdb004

identity_algorithm.scope: TICKER-SCOPED (Product Decision 2) -- ticker is part of the hashed canonical representation; two structures for different tickers never collide.
identity_algorithm.matching: EXACT CANONICAL MATCH ONLY (Product Decision 3) -- no embeddings, no LLM similarity, no fuzzy/heuristic matching. Two structures share a phi_id only when their JSON-canonicalized representation is byte-identical before hashing.
identity_algorithm.formula: phi_id = sha256(json.dumps({identity_version, ticker, alpha_id, taxonomy_version, taxonomy_sha256, chain_edges}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True))
identity_algorithm.chain_edges_definition: The deterministically sorted SET of (source_node_id, edge_type, target_node_id) triples among this run's structure_graph.json edges whose edge['alpha_ids'] already includes this alpha_id -- reused verbatim from the existing, already-persisted edge/alpha linkage, never re-derived.
identity_algorithm.digest_function: hashlib.sha256 over a JSON-canonicalized (sorted keys, fixed separators, ASCII) representation -- stable across processes and Python versions, unlike Python's own hash().
identity_algorithm.taxonomy_authority_source: Each run's OWN persisted tradingagents_comqutor_vocabulary_snapshot.json (taxonomy_version/taxonomy_sha256) -- never recomputed against whatever the current worktree's taxonomy file happens to be, so a historical run's phi_id stays stable even if the taxonomy has since changed. A taxonomy/version difference between two runs automatically produces different phi_ids (Product Decision 4) -- verified by test.

canonical_chain_boundary_rule.rule: For one (ticker, alpha_id) pair, the canonical chain is the SET of that run's (source, edge_type, target) edge triples already linked to alpha_id via the Structure Graph's own existing edge['alpha_ids'] field -- not a single linear PATH.
canonical_chain_boundary_rule.why_not_a_linear_path: The persisted Structure Graph does not disambiguate one canonical path when an alpha's linked edges branch or span more than one connected component. Selecting 'the' path would require an arbitrary tie-breaking rule this implementation refuses to invent, per the explicit instruction not to invent graph semantics.
canonical_chain_boundary_rule.why_this_is_the_narrowest_supported_unit: Requires no path-search algorithm, no cycle handling, no branch-selection heuristic -- purely a deterministic set-membership filter over already-existing, already-persisted data. For the common case of a single linear chain (the Development Plan's own worked example), a single path's edge set and its edge sequence carry identical information, so this rule IS a genuine chain identity in that case.
canonical_chain_boundary_rule.known_limitation_reported_honestly: Two runs whose linked edges represent the same abstract multi-hop causal idea but decompose into a different literal edge structure (e.g. an extra intermediate node appears in one run's LLM extraction but not the other's) will receive DIFFERENT phi_ids under this rule -- confirmed empirically: the two real NVDA smoke-test runs from this session (2f8ee897 and c9abf687) share ZERO phi_ids despite both being genuine NVDA research runs, because their independently-extracted claim sets produced different literal edges. This is EXACT canonical matching working exactly as specified (Product Decision 3), not a bug -- but it does mean this v1 will under-recognize real-world recurrence whenever independent LLM extraction produces even slightly different literal structure. This limitation is inherent to 'exact match only' and was anticipated in the authorized Phase 2 spec's collision-risk section.

ticker_scope_rule: Ticker is a first-class field in the hashed canonical representation (Product Decision 2). NVDA's AI_DEMAND->GPU_SHORTAGE chain and AMD's identical-shaped chain never receive the same phi_id -- verified by test_same_chain_different_ticker_produces_different_phi_id.

versioning_rule.identity_version: alpha_memory.phi.v1 -- a bump to this string is required before any change to what gets hashed; a version bump never silently reinterprets a previously-computed phi_id.
versioning_rule.taxonomy_version_and_sha256: Read per-run from that run's own persisted vocabulary snapshot; included in every hash so a taxonomy change never silently merges historical structures across the boundary.

db_migration.reasoning: Every input (structure_graph.json's edges/alpha_ids, tradingagents_comqutor_vocabulary_snapshot.json's taxonomy fields, metadata.json's ticker/created_at) already exists, already persisted, for every run. The cross-run reader performs a filesystem directory scan under output_root, matching this codebase's own existing pattern of pure-file-based offline/audit code paths (e.g. this session's earlier offline-replay-proof tests). No new column, table, or migration was added or is needed for this SHADOW-only v1.
db_migration.performance_note_not_a_migration: A full per-ticker directory scan on every run_audit.json build is O(number of persisted runs for that ticker) -- acceptable at today's data volume, and explicitly NOT a reason to add a DB index/table now per the instruction to only migrate if implementation PROVES it strictly necessary. If ticker run counts grow much larger, a future step MAY want a DB-backed index -- that is an explicit, separate, future decision, not made here.
